advances: The selected three cylindrical caps of an actual planar-fiber family. The core conclusion concerns cap budgets and mass under an explicit nonradial motion.

proof:
The determinants of the two endpoint linear maps are $1+3t^2>0$. Their endpoint vertices are obtained from those of $T$ by adding or subtracting respectively $t(1,-1)$, $t(0,1)$ and $t(-1,0)$. The lifted hull has only the three specified integer bases, and its middle fiber is their Minkowski midpoint by the equal endpoint coefficients at base zero. The six middle vertices in counterclockwise order are
$$
(-1/3-t,1/6+t/2),\ (-1/3,-1/3),\
(1/6+t/2,-1/3-t),\ (2/3,-1/3),\
(1/6+t/2,1/6+t/2),\ (-1/3,2/3).
$$
Each is one of the nine endpoint vertex averages. The determinants of an oriented edge of this list with a displacement from its initial point to one of those nine averages are among
$$
0,\quad t,\quad (1+3t^2)/4,\quad
(1+t)(1+3t)/4,\quad (1+t)/2,\quad (1-t)(1+3t)/4.
$$
They are nonnegative and each successive turn is positive. Thus the listed polygon is their hull. Shoelace gives area $(1+3t)/2$ for the middle, and the determinants give endpoint areas $(1+3t^2)/2$.

The determinant-one map $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(-x_1-x_2,x_1)$ commutes with $J$ and cyclically permutes both the vertices of $T$ and the displayed cap margins. Thus it suffices to compute the $x_1\ge0$ mass. At an endpoint the cap retains the vertex with $x_1=2/3$ and cuts the other two edges at relative lengths $(2/3)/(1-t)$ and $(2/3)/(1+t)$. Its fraction is their product. In the middle the line $x_1=0$ meets the polygon at heights $\pm(1+3t)/[3(1+t)]$. These two intersections and the three positive-$x_1$ vertices give cap area $(1+3t)(2+3t)/[9(1+t)]$ by shoelace. Summing the three masses gives the displayed $D(t)$. The cap margins sum to zero. The original three vertices of $T$, all of which remain in the middle fiber, are private strict witnesses for their respective caps. Positive dilation preserves these incidences.

Differentiation gives $R'(t)$ with denominator $27(1-t^2)^2(1+t+2t^2)^2$ and numerator
$$
2[1+4t(3-t)+44t^3+9t^4(5-2t^2)+48t^5]>0.
$$
Hence $q(t)$ lies strictly between $M(t_0)/M(t)$ and $D(t_0)/D(t)$, and commutes with the actual Minkowski midpoint when used as a squared scale. The new total and cap masses are $(M(t_0)+D(t_0)/R(t))/2$ and $(M(t_0)R(t)+D(t_0))/2$. Their strict first-order signs follow from $R'(t_0)>0$. Any homothety taking $A_{t_0}$ to the dilated $A_t$ about zero must have the prescribed common dilation because the maximum first coordinate is $2/3$ before scaling. The second coordinate at its unique maximizing vertex changes with $t$, so that homothety cannot realize the motion. Finally substituting $t=9/100$ and squared scale $(1007/1000)^2$ gives new mass $16826115057/10000000000$ and cap mass $2271685752437/2975700000000$. Subtraction from the old values $42/25$ and $6811/8910$ gives the two exact changes.

statement:
Let $T=\operatorname{conv}\{(-1/3,-1/3),(2/3,-1/3),(-1/3,2/3)\}$ and $J=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-1&-2\\2&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. For $0<t<1/3$ put $A_t=(I+tJ)T$, $B_t=(I-tJ)T$ and $D_t=(A_t+B_t)/2$. Use these at integer bases $-1,0,1$ as the actual fibers of their lifted convex hull. Their total area and the common raw mass in each of the three fixed cylindrical caps $-x_1-x_2\ge0$, $x_1\ge0$, $x_2\ge0$ are
$$
M(t)=\tfrac32(1+t+2t^2),\qquad
D(t)=\frac{6+7t+12t^2-9t^3}{9(1-t^2)}.
$$
The caps form an inclusion-minimal cover. The ratio $R(t)=D(t)/M(t)$ strictly increases. For each $t_0\in(0,1/3)$ and $t<t_0$, dilate all three fibers by the positive factor whose square is
$$
q(t)=\tfrac12\bigl(M(t_0)/M(t)+D(t_0)/D(t)\bigr).
$$
This preserves actual midpoint compatibility and the selected cap planes. The total mass increases and each selected cap mass strictly decreases relative to $t_0$, with strict first-order changes as $t_0-t$ increases from zero. The motion is nonradial about zero. At $t_0=1/10$ a finite rational witness instead uses $t=9/100$ and dilation $1007/1000$, giving mass increase $26115057/10000000000$ and common cap-mass drop $892421526211/883782900000000$.
title: A coordinated unrotation strictly lowers every selected cap budget of the planar core
